TLDR: While the parkour remains excellent, nearly everything else feels like a step back from Dying Light 1. PROS: ➕Parkour is great ➕Story-driven choices that impact the narrative outcome CONS: ➖Enemy AI seems buggy and occasionally just “Shuts off” ➖Excessive pointless zombie spawns - literally 3 melee attacks suddenly spawns multiple fast infected ➖Sorting in inventory never saves ➖Narrative isn’t that interesting ➖Most quests are boring fetch quests ➖Obnoxious and constant audio cues that you cannot disable (constantly notifies of ANY nearby event) ➖Combat skill tree is boring My review for Dying Light (DL1) is here Content (Game world/Narrative) – [4/10] The game world takes place in a city called Villedor in 2036, 22 years after the events of DL1. The setting is mostly similar to Harran, the city from DL1. There are two main areas, a smaller village-like starting area that is a bit more rural, and the city proper, with larger buildings and a downtown-like area. Regardless of the differences, every building interior looks like every other and no matter how sheltered or locked down a place has been for decades, there’s always somehow zombies waiting for you inside. The exploration is good, and there are tons of random things to do in the open world. Think like an Ubisoft game, and all the good, and bad, that comes with it. The narrative to me was a big let down. You play as Aiden who is a “Pilgrim”. Basically what Dying Light has branded to be some sort of long-distance parkour enthusiast deliverymen. Aiden has come to Villedor to find his sister and thus begins the search. The story is just all over the place. I really like how there are (seemingly) big decision points to make, but these don’t seem to have a big effect on the story other than some slightly different cutscenes, dialogue, and the ending cutscene. I got about 20 hours into it before I was starting to get bored of the disappointing fetch quest side missions, and the main story itself. While there are some revelations near the end, the story never hit a positive note after dragging on. Gameplay (Mechanics/Difficulty) – [5/10] The general gameplay loop is typical of an open world game - completing mission objectives from one area to another. Coming from DL1, there are some big changes, and most of them are not positive. The parkour remains the best part of the game, by far., and I think it’s improved a bit. Jumping from the top of towers still gives that white-knuckle tense feeling, so it’s still great there. Adding to the already good traversal mechanics are the paraglider and a grappling hook. Though DL1 had a grappling hook, it’s not bound to a talent, you get it about 60% of the way through the story. The night elements have also changed. Now, you have a timer that forces you to either use a consumable or reach a UV light before it runs out, else its game over. The RPG-like gear system has been expanded from just weapons to include gear. I didn’t find this very meaningful and the game could have done without it. Speaking of talents, there are two trees - combat and parkour. The combat tree I found terribly boring, but the parkour tree was good. The difficulty is more on the easier side. The few times I died were all because of failed parkour attempts and not the combat. Though with the combat, the Volatiles will still mess you up. The regular zombies are just a hindrance, and often annoying as the runners constantly show up when doing basic attacks against any enemy Technical (Graphics/Performance) – [5/10] I found the graphics to be this weird middle area between PS4 and PS4-era fidelity. The environments and world look great, if repetitive, but the character design and animations are a step lower. I played fully maxed and felt the performance was good. Of note is the constant bugs. I hear this has been improved with post-launch patches, but I still ran into things constantly. The most egregious is the enemy AI. The AI would occasionally literally “Turn off” and the enemies would just stand there. Also the Volatile chase sequences were a bit of a joke with how poor the AI is at following you 1440p @ 240hz | installed on SSD Audio – [4/10] The music wasn’t great. In fact, I ended up turning it down because it was getting annoying. There’s also a sound effect, like sort of deep “Ding” that plays when an event near you is active, which happens all the time . I couldn’t find a way to turn it off, but it really takes you out of the game with the constant sound. The voice acting is good. Replay Factor (Longevity) – [6/10] There is NG+ and achievements. Perhaps the big draw would be co-op and the choices available within the campaign, even if they are a bit lackluster. Still, I think there’s some good replay value here. Final Verdict – [5/10] Dying Light 2 (DL2) simply isn’t a great game. It lacks something that made DL1 so special. If I had to attribute this downfall to features specifically, it would be the narrative, and the lack of nighttime danger. DL1 didn’t really have an amazing story, mind you, but the narrative here is just terrible. As I got closer to the end, it was a struggle to push on and finish when I just didn’t care about any of the characters or the ending. While I like the touch of adding major decisions to certain parts of the story, even the outcomes just weren’t exciting enough to push the narrative to anything above mid-tier. As for the nighttime danger, it’s sad because the game is literally called Dying Light . In the first game, nighttime often shifted the game from being an action game into a horror game. The tension and change were dramatic and noticeable. I never got the same feeling here. In DL2 night time is more of a stealth or parkour chase in the open world, or rummaging through samey-looking buildings due to the dangerous infected being outside. Even if you are spotted by a Volatile and a chase sequence begins, the AI is so dumb that it simply can’t keep up with the player. As long as you keep moving, there’s really nothing to fear. Just like DL1 though, the parkour continues to impress, and I do really like the traversal elements. But damn, if I only cared about the world at all. This is a hard one to recommend. As with most 5’s, I often struggle to recommend or not. In the end, I’m going to go with a recommendation. I love DL1, first-person games, RPG mechanics, and zombie games, so my love for the gameplay elements kept me interested enough to finish it, but barely. I would only recommend this if you loved DL1, and even then, prepare to be disappointed. Recommend? (Price) [Y/N] Yes $60 is steep. I wouldn’t pay over $15 for this game.
